name: Caspe – battle of March 1938
story: From 1936 Caspe was the seat of the anarchist-led Regional Defence Council of Aragon, which ran the collectivised Republican part of the region. In August 1937 the Republican government dissolved the council by force and arrested its president, Joaquín Ascaso. During the Aragon offensive three divisions of Yagüe's Moroccan Army Corps reached Caspe on 15 March 1938. International Brigades XI, XIII and XV, later joined by the XII and XIV, defended the town, the XV Brigade most stubbornly. Caspe fell on 17 March and became a Nationalist corps headquarters for the Ebro front.
see: The historic town centre and the hills around the Guadalope valley where the brigades fought. Traces are scattered and mostly unmarked.
plan: Start from the old town and the tourist office. A local guide or book helps to locate the battle positions.
